_doc: Per-language recommendations for span_extension.py's opt-in flags (definite_trigger, relation_trigger, typology_fallback, typology_fallback_articles) — Step 1/2 of internal-docs/aim1-typology-source-structure-plan.md. Every flag defaults to OFF (same as no entry at all here); a language gets `true` for a flag only once someone has actually scored it against real gold and found the flag worth keeping — never added speculatively. This is the SAME 'measure once, remember it in one line, no code edit' pattern config/gold_langs.json and config/typology/directions.json already use. `span_extension.extend_spans`'s own function-level defaults are `None` (meaning 'consult this file'); passing an explicit True/False as a Python arg or CLI flag always overrides whatever is recorded here, for a one-off experiment without touching the config. See span_extension.py's own module docstring for the full measured numbers behind every entry below — this file only records the VERDICT, not the evidence. `typology_fallback_articles` (added 2026-09-27, D4a follow-up): SEPARATE from `typology_fallback` — gates only the 'articles' RISK_RULES noun/name-extension mechanism. NOT the same story as `typology_fallback` itself: a DEEPER bug was found during this follow-up — `analyze_language.py`'s own existence pre-check for 'articles'/'case_marking'/'possession_affix' had been left calling the OLD `typology.direction()` table directly, never updated when D4a moved `span_extension.py`'s own direction lookups onto `gram_struct.merged_direction()`. Fixed (`analyze_language.py`) so gram_struct is now consulted consistently everywhere — but fixing it makes 'articles' risk newly DISCOVERABLE for spa/ben/asm (previously unreachable regardless of `typology_fallback`, since the old table had no article-order parameter for them at all). `typology_fallback_articles` exists specifically so that newly-discoverable capability doesn't silently activate an unmeasured mechanism — see spa's own dedicated measurement below.

spa._note: measured 2026-09-24 (whole Bible, Clear gold, WITH the identity guard): net positive on the conflict-aware ledger, 4,435 improvements vs 3,561 real conflicts. Aggregate F1 still reads as a drop (.774->.729) because most of the reported 'regression' is the gold-unclaimed-article metric artifact documented in span_extension.py's fra section, not a real quality loss — see that module's own docstring, not this note, for the full account.
spa._articles_note: DEDICATED MEASUREMENT 2026-09-27 (D4a follow-up). CORRECTION to an earlier same-day analysis: the `spanext_noun_before`/`spanext_name_before` pairs (25,737 / 14,767 triggered) are NOT driven by the 'articles' risk at all -- verified directly (analyze() on live spa data returned only case_marking/possession_affix findings until the analyze_language.py fix below) and by a byte-for-byte diff of spa's ENTIRE spanext output before vs after D4a's span_extension.py/gram_struct.py changes: IDENTICAL. Those pairs come from `case_marking` (the adposition direction, 'before' for spa, UNCHANGED old vs new backend) -- i.e. this is spa's PRE-EXISTING, already-shipped 2026-09-24 mechanism, not something D4a activated. D4a's OWN fix caused zero change to span_extension's output for spa/ben/asm. HOWEVER, isolating that pre-existing mechanism's real precision (splitting conflicts into the already-documented gold-non-credit-of-articles artifact -- de/la/los/el/las etc., ~64% of conflicts, not counted as errors -- vs genuine content-word steals) found artifact-corrected precision of only 40.8% (noun_before, 3,446/8,440) and 37.9% (name_before, 887/2,338) -- well below the ~2/3 bar the nominally similar mechanism cleared for eng (F1 .632->.741). Real conflicts are mostly genealogy name-list steals ('Chûs' wrongly extended onto the next unrelated name in a list) and genitive-construct steals ('tierra'/'siervo'/'su obra' grabbing an unrelated adjacent content word). This calls the ORIGINAL 'net positive, 4,435 vs 3,561' verdict's cleanliness into some question -- worth a fuller re-audit of case_marking's own conflict bucket someday -- but is independent of D4a and NOT itself acted on here (typology_fallback stays true, unchanged, pending that separate investigation). SEPARATELY: fixing analyze_language.py's own existence-check bug (see this file's `_doc`) made the true 'articles' risk newly reachable for spa for the first time ever (previously unreachable under ANY backend, old or new) -- confirmed empirically post-fix (analyze() now returns 'articles' findings for noun/name). Verified this newly-reachable-but-UNMEASURED mechanism does NOT fire: `typology_fallback_articles: false` (no entry->off) keeps span_extension's spa output byte-identical to the pre-fix baseline even after the analyze_language.py fix. Kept OFF pending its own dedicated measurement, exactly like every other never-yet-scored flag in this file.

ben._note: measured 2026-09-24 (whole Bible, Clear gold, WITH the identity guard): still net negative on the conflict-aware ledger, 87 improvements vs 217 real conflicts (down from 427/1,355 before the guard — an ~84% reduction in harm, but not a flip to positive). Kept OFF; revisit if the pronoun-stealing gap span_extension.py documents ever gets a further fix.

asm._note: measured 2026-09-24 (whole Bible, Clear gold, WITH the identity guard): same pattern as ben, smaller scale (115 vs 258 real conflicts before the guard). Kept OFF.

hin._note: measured 2026-09-24 (whole OT, Clear gold, isolated to the possessor-only pairs, WITH the chain-boundary fix): a small, real, incomplete improvement — 47 correct / 76 real conflict / 41 gold-unclaimed / 137 no-gold-link, vs 47/79/43/142 without the chain-boundary fix. Kept ON since it measured no worse than off and is the one place this session found ANY positive signal for the construct-chain problem; the harder cases (neither chain member aligned yet) are still unresolved — see span_extension.py's own docstring.
hin._definite_note: not applicable to hin — Hindi has no article_order direction at all (GB022/023 both 0), so definite_trigger has nothing to fire on regardless of this setting.

eng._note: measured 2026-09-24 (whole OT, Clear gold): aggregate F1 unchanged (.646->.646); of 401 triggered pairs, 391 had no checkable gold link at all and 0 of the remaining 10 were correct — no evidence of value as built, plausibly because the proper-name rule in compute_definite dominates its output. Kept OFF.
